attributes.name: [OpenRouter] Cache Hit Rate Drop
attributes.description: Alerts when the average cache hit rate of any model drops below a configurable threshold. A sudden drop in cache hit rate can signal prompt changes, model switching, or cache invalidation events that increase effective token cost.

investigation_guide.blob:
## Cache Hit Rate Drop

### Triage Steps
1. Open the OpenRouter Performance dashboard and inspect the cache hit rate trend.
2. Check which models experienced the drop:
   `FROM metrics-openrouter.performance-* | STATS rate = AVG(openrouter.performance.cache_hit_rate) BY openrouter.performance.model | SORT rate ASC`
3. Correlate with prompt changes in your application — cache hits depend on prompt prefix stability.
4. Check whether a new model was introduced that does not support prompt caching.

### Common Causes
- Prompt prefix changes that invalidate the cache (e.g., dynamic system prompts with timestamps)
- New model rollout where the model does not support prompt caching
- Shift in traffic to a provider that does not cache
- Very short prompts below the minimum caching threshold

### Tuning
- Lower the threshold (e.g., `0.1` = 10%) if your workload naturally has low cache reuse.
